result.topic_en: Euler uses spherical trigonometry to set up the equation fixing the moment during a lunar eclipse when the Moon and the shadow centre are equally far from the node, expressed through the angle ρ between the lunar orbit and the ecliptic.
result.transcription:
De loco lunae ex eclipsibus lunaribus determinando. 367
orbitae[?] quem tabulae lunares indicare debent, neque ad hoc reductione loci lunae ad eclipticam opus[?] habebimus, uti vera oppositio postulat.
§. 7. Repraesentet ergo arcus $\sigma\lambda$ non veram oppositionem, sed eum luminarium situm, in quo arcus[?] $☊\lambda$ aequalis sit arcui $☊\sigma$, hocque eveniat elapsis post initium $SL$ horis $t$. Sit ergo hoc momento tam longitudo umbrae, quam longitudo lunae in orbita a nodo computata $☊\sigma = ☊\lambda = x$, erit[?] ob $S\sigma = (m+k)\,t''$, $L\lambda = (n+k)\,t''$, arcus $☊S = x-(m+k)\,t''$ et arcus $☊L = x-(n+k)\,t''$. Deinde[?] vero erit arcus $☊s = x+(m+k)\,(h-t)''$ et $☊l = x+(n+k)\,(h-t)''$. Ponatur angulus[?] $\lambda☊\sigma = \varrho$, erit ex natura triangulorum sphaericorum
$\cos SL = \cos\varrho \sin ☊L \sin ☊S + \cos ☊L \cos ☊S,\quad \cos sl = \cos\varrho \sin ☊l \sin ☊s + \cos ☊l \cos ☊s.$
Quare cum sit $SL = sl$, erit
$\cos ☊L \cos ☊S - \cos ☊l \cos ☊s = \cos\varrho\,(\sin ☊l \sin ☊s - \sin ☊L \sin ☊S).$
§. 8. Est vero per compositionem angulorum ut sequitur
$\cos ☊L = \cos x \cos (n+k)\,t'' + \sin x \sin (n+k)\,t''$
$\cos ☊S = \cos x \cos (m+k)\,t'' + \sin x \sin (m+k)\,t''$
$\cos ☊l = \cos x \cos (n+k)\,(h-t)'' - \sin x \sin (n+k)\,(h-t)''$
$\cos ☊s = \cos x \cos (m+k)\,(h-t)'' - \sin x \sin (m+k)\,(h-t)''$
$\sin ☊l = \sin x \cos (n+k)\,(h-t)'' + \cos x \sin (n+k)\,(h-t)''$
$\sin ☊s = \sin x \cos (m+k)\,(h-t)'' + \cos x \sin (m+k)\,(h-t)''$
$\sin ☊L = \sin x \cos (n+k)\,t'' - \cos x \sin (n+k)\,t''$
$\sin ☊S = \sin x \cos (m+k)\,t'' - \cos x \sin (m+k)\,t''$
seu per alias sinuum proprietates
$\cos ☊L \cos ☊S = \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊S - ☊L) + \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊S + ☊L)$
$\cos ☊l \cos ☊s = \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊l - ☊s) + \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊s + ☊l)$
$\sin ☊l \sin ☊s = \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊l - ☊s) - \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊s + ☊l)$
$\sin ☊L \sin ☊S = \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊S - ☊L) - \tfrac{1}{2}\cos(☊S + ☊L).$
§. 9. Cum igitur sit
$☊S - ☊L = (n-m)\,t'' \qquad ☊S + ☊L = 2x - (m+n+2k)\,t''$
$☊l - ☊s = (n-m)\,(h-t)'' \qquad ☊s + ☊l = 2x + (m+n+2k)\,(h-t)''.$
His ergo valoribus substitutis reperiemus
$\left.\begin{array}{l} +\cos(n-m)t'' + \cos(2x-(m+n+2k)\,t'') \\ -\cos(n-m)(h-t)'' - \cos(2x+(m+n+2k)(h-t)'') \end{array}\right\} = \cos\varrho \left\{\begin{array}{l} \cos(n-m)(h-t)'' - \cos(2x+(m+n+2k)(h-t)'') \\ -\cos(n-m)t'' + \cos(2x-(m+n+2k)\,t'') \end{array}\right.$
quae reducta abit in
$(1+\cos\varrho)\,(\cos(n-m)t'' - \cos(n-m)(h-t)'') = (1-\cos\varrho)\,(\cos(2x+(m+n+2k)(h-t)'') - \cos(2x-(m+n+2k)\,t'')).$

items.quote: Repraesentet ergo arcus $\sigma\lambda$ non veram oppositionem, sed eum luminarium situm, in quo arcus[?] $☊\lambda$ aequalis sit arcui $☊\sigma$, hocque eveniat elapsis post initium $SL$ horis $t$.
items.english: Let the arc σλ therefore represent not the true opposition, but that position of the luminaries in which the arc ☊λ equals the arc ☊σ, and let this occur t hours after the beginning SL.
